subject: Request: Amend service guarantees for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Noah Parker <noah.parker@elysianhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Elysian Legal <legal@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Request: service guarantee language for private VPC

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with Redwood for our private VPC deployment in our colo facility, but our procurement and risk teams are asking for a narrow amendment to the SLA language around uptime and latency guarantees when the control plane is customer-hosted.

High level asks from Elysian:
- We need a written carve-out that absolves Redwood of credits when downtime is demonstrably caused by our on-prem networking, power, or virtualization fabric failures.
- We still need a latency SLO for inference tail latency (P95) delivered by Redwood agent-managed serving components: target 150ms P95 for 16k-context chat workloads.
- We require a monitoring and incident evidence process: what telemetry logs and alerts will Redwood produce to validate downtime or latency breaches?

I've attached our architecture diagram and a short SOC2/RFC doc for context. Can you propose contract language and the operational checklist Redwood will rely on to determine responsibility?

Appreciate a quick outline so I can get the legal team unblocked.

Best,
Noah
Director of Engineering
Elysian Health

Attachments: elysian-architecture-diagram.pdf (image/pdf), elysian-soc2-rfc.docx (docx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Noah Parker <noah.parker@elysianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: service guarantee language for private VPC

Noah — thanks for the clear ask and the artifacts. We're excited to make this deployment work. Below is a pragmatic approach that balances our ability to guarantee runtime behavior while acknowledging customer-controlled infrastructure.

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Shared-responsibility carve-outs: Redwood will not provide uptime credits for events caused by the customer-managed environment (power, rack-level network, local hypervisor failures, third-party colo network outages) provided the customer supplies post-incident evidence per the checklist below.
2) Latency SLO (service component boundary): Redwood will commit to P95 inference tail latency <= 150ms for specified model families and sequence lengths when the Redwood agent + local serving stack report: (a) agent-heartbeat present, (b) KV cache warm, (c) no local resource contention flagged.
3) Evidence & telemetry: Redwood will publish a standardized evidence checklist (agent logs, heartbeats, kernel-level CPU/mem metrics, sample request traces, and router/egress metrics) and will accept customer-provided facility incident reports.
4) Operational governance: a 30-day post-deployment observability period where both sides calibrate thresholds; final SLO effective after calibration.

I attached a short draft of proposed SLO language (high level) and an operational evidence checklist — this is intended to be a starting point for legal. I'll pull in Laura for contract language and Rishi for the telemetry requirements.

Vivek
VP Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-slo-amendment-ELY.pdf (pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Noah Parker <noah.parker@elysianhealth.com>, Elysian Legal <legal@elysianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: service guarantee language for private VPC

Team — quick legal notes on the draft:
- We can accept carve-outs for customer-controlled infra, but we need the contract to require timely evidence submission (within 14 days) and an agreed format.
- We should limit the carve-out to operational causes (power, network, virtualization). We'll not accept customer claims that are vague — the checklist should be exhaustive enough to support/deny a credit.
- Credit cap: propose a maximum monthly service credit of 10% of the monthly managed fee for any single month, with overall cap of 25% per 12-month period.
- Incident classification process: include a 3-step dispute resolution (initial review by ops, joint postmortem, final arbitration by an independent technical reviewer if needed).

Noah — can you confirm Elysian is comfortable with the 14-day evidence window and the proposed caps? If so we'll incorporate into the redline.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Noah Parker <noah.parker@elysianhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: service guarantee language for private VPC

Hi Noah — technical follow-up on telemetry and enforcement:

What Redwood requires to validate an uptime or latency breach when running in customer-hosted mode:
- Agent heartbeat stream (with millisecond timestamps) for the serving cluster for the 72-hour window around the incident.
- Per-node CPU, GPU, memory, and disk-utilization samples at 1-min granularity for 24 hours before and after the incident peak.
- Router ingress/egress latency histograms and packet-drop counters for the affected period.
- A sample of request traces (redwood trace id, request timings, model id, sequence length) for at least 200 requests spanning the incident window.
- Colo facility incident report (ticket id, description, start/end times, and root cause if available).

Operational notes:
- We will not assert credits if agent-heartbeat is missing at any time during the incident window. If heartbeats stop because of a network partition, we will use heartbeats + router metrics + facility report to determine responsibility.
- For the latency SLO we measure from arrival at the Redwood agent to final token emission (so local queuing and host-level interference are captured).
- During the 30-day calibration, Rishi's team will run synthetic probes and share baseline P95 percentiles; after calibration, the SLO will be updated to reflect measured behavior.

If Elysian can provide the heartbeat stream and the facility ticketing export as part of the incident packet, validation is straightforward. Happy to schedule a quick runbook session.

—Rishi
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: service guarantee language for private VPC

Looping back with a commercial proposal to present to Noah and Elysian Legal:
- Accept the shared-responsibility carve-out with the 14-day evidence requirement.
- Redwood will commit to P95 <= 150ms for the agreed model family after the 30-day calibration window.
- Commercially, propose a 10% monthly credit cap and 25% annual cap (per Laura).
- Requested sign-off path: legal redline (Laura) + 2-week calibration + then execution of an amendment to the Master Services Agreement.

Can we greenlight this as our standard amendment for colo/private deployments? If so I will send Noah a draft amendment and the onboarding runbook link.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Elysian Legal is OK with the 14-day evidence window and the proposed credit caps as long as the evidence checklist is comprehensive and non-discriminatory. They'll send a short redline, but I don't expect big changes.

Next steps on our side:
- I'll have infra runbook and the facility ticketing export ready within 7 days when we sign the amendment.
- Please schedule the 90-minute calibration workshop (Rishi suggested synthetic probes during the window).
- Once Laura and Elysian Legal exchange redlines, we can route to procurement and finalize the amendment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Noah
